### J-1 Worker text is copied verbatim into a memory record with no handling of hostile content
- quote: "the first two under `## What is wrong`, the third under `## Proposed change`"
- quote: "each of the three texts appears verbatim under its section"
- situation (adversary): a worker is an untrusted writer. Its `change_request` holds a line like `## Proposed change`, a `---` front-matter delimiter, or a fake `Status: decided`. It may also be empty, or megabytes long.
- fix: add an AC for hostile and empty `change_request` texts. Either neutralise heading and front-matter lines, or refuse the handoff loudly. State the size bound and the concurrent-run behaviour (one record).
- validation: confirmed: FR-2 and AC-2 require verbatim copy of worker text under fixed headings. Nothing in the spec handles heading, front-matter or empty text, so a `change_request` containing `## Proposed change` would break the record's sections and the memory check that AC-1 depends on.
- disposition: spec-fix by agent: Delegated grill (human: run the whole flow on recommended): FR-16, AC-20, AC-21: block refuses a change_request text with a '## ' or '---' line, or an empty text, and files nothing; it already files under the effort lock (RF-17); size noted in Risks.

### J-2 A deferral can remove every test requirement from a task, and nothing checks the target is real
- quote: "then red is accepted with no file requirement"
- quote: "A TC a later task proves only in part counts as deferred"
- quote: "fail for a deferred TC ID that the task its `Test:` line names doesn't cite as its own"
- situation (adversary): UJ-2's misuse is "the command names an unrelated file only to get past the check".
- fix: have FR-12 also require that the target task exists and is later. Say which reading wins when a TC is both own and deferred. Decide whether a task may defer all of its TCs (AC-6) and what stops that being a bypass. Re-check the target when tasks are removed.
- validation: confirmed: FR-12 only requires that the named task cites the TC as its own. It does not require that task to be later than the deferring one, and nothing says which reading wins when a TC is both own and deferred on the same line. AC-6 lets a task defer every TC it cites, which removes its file requirement. A nonexistent target is probably caught, since it cites nothing, so the "target is real" part of the finding is weaker than the rest.
- disposition: spec-fix by agent: Delegated grill (human: run the whole flow on recommended): FR-3, AC-23: a TC cited outside the deferral part is own (own wins); deferring every TC is caught at the tasks jury (Risks); the later-task check moved out with #69 (non-goals).

### J-3 Tasks under Fixes bypass approval, and a judged task can be moved there
- quote: "keep it approved when a task is added under `#### Fixes`"
- quote: "without making a lens re-run on that alone"
- situation (adversary): FR-8 and FR-7 let any task under `#### Fixes` go through with no juror verdict and no re-approval. Nothing bounds the number or scope of such tasks, so unreviewed work accumulates under an approved gate.
- fix: define "added under Fixes" as an ID never seen at the judged version. Treat a changed or moved judged ID as a normal change that triggers a re-run. Say who may add fix tasks and whether a limit applies.
- validation: refuted: The Decisions entry ("shown to the juror but doesn't make a lens re-run or withdraw an approval") and FR-8 [research: RF-9] make this behaviour deliberate. The Glossary defines a fix task as "added after the tasks gate judged the list", which settles that it is a new task. Unbounded accumulation is a design choice, not a contradiction or gap in the artefact.

### J-4 With NIO_PERF off, the speed requirement is enforced nowhere
- quote: "assert its time limit only when `NIO_PERF=1` is set"
- quote: "without any wall-clock limit that load can exceed"
- situation (adversary): after this change the status-speed and drift-speed limits are never asserted in the default run. No AC, FR or entry says where `NIO_PERF=1` is run (CI, a scheduled run, before release). A 10x slowdown of `nio flow status` then passes every review and gate, and the "NFR-3: status in under 2 seconds" requirement quietly loses its only check.
- fix: name one place and one trigger where `NIO_PERF=1` runs, with an AC for it. Narrow FR-11 to the named speed assertions, or list which timing checks remain.
- validation: merged: same as J-9

### J-5 The evaluator's "only rating lines" rule is enforced by the card and tool choice alone
- quote: "change only the tasks' `Tier:`, `Effort:` and `Mode:` lines in `tasks.md`"
- quote: "with an edit tool and no whole-file write tool"
- situation (adversary): the evaluator reads task text that workers and drafters wrote, so injected text in a task could steer it. An edit tool can still change any line, such as a task's `Test:` or `Files:` line. Edits keyed on a repeated `Tier: standard` line can also land on the wrong task silently.
- fix: add a deterministic post-run check, for example that the diff of `tasks.md` touches only rating lines, run by `nio check tasks` or the flow, with an AC that rejects a stray edit.
- validation: merged: same as J-18

### J-6 Own TC IDs: refuse when any file is missing, or only when none is named
- quote: "→ refused, naming the missing file; an attempt is used"
- quote: "IF `nio flow red` refuses a command for naming none of the required test files THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL name only the required files in the refusal."
- situation (logic): a task's `Test:` line cites own TC-10 and TC-12, which have different files, and the red command names only TC-10's file. The decision table row `own | no` refuses it for TC-12's missing file and spends an attempt. FR-4 refuses only a command naming none of the required files, so this command is accepted. The same input gets two outcomes. AC-5 only covers one own TC, so it settles neither reading.
- fix: say whether the command must name every required file or at least one. Make the table row, FR-4 and FR-3 use the same wording, and add an AC with two own TC IDs.
- validation: confirmed: The decision table row `own | no` refuses for any missing own file, while FR-4 speaks of a command "naming none of the required test files". With two own TC IDs and only one file named, the two readings give different outcomes. AC-4 and AC-5 cover only one own TC and settle neither.
- disposition: spec-fix by agent: Delegated grill (human: run the whole flow on recommended): FR-3, FR-4, red table: the command must name a file of at least one own TC ID, as today; AC-22 covers two own TCs.

### J-7 Fix-task rows say "shown and listed", but FR-7 and FR-8 add "no re-run", which the table and ACs don't carry
- quote: "→ shown in the fix-check pack and listed by `changed`"
- quote: "without making a lens re-run on that alone"
- quote: "then T-30 is among the changed IDs it reports"
- situation (logic): the only change since the judged version is T-30 added under `#### Fixes`. `nio jury changed` lists T-30 as a changed ID, exactly as it lists an added task outside Fixes, which the table treats the same way. Nothing says what separates "listed, no re-run" from "listed, re-run". AC-10 tests only that the gate stays approved. Nothing tests that no lens is asked to re-run, and nothing covers a Fixes task together with a removal. In AC-8, T-4 is removed while the gate is approved. FR-8 covers only an add under Fixes, so it does not say whether that removal withdraws the approval.
- fix: add a column to the decision table for "makes a lens re-run" (no for Fixes, yes for the other rows). Add an AC for a Fixes-only change that asserts no re-run. State what happens to approval when a task is removed.
- validation: merged: same as J-15

### J-8 FR-11 bans any load-exceedable time limit, but FR-15 and the Decisions entry keep some
- quote: "THE SYSTEM SHALL decide the result without any wall-clock limit that load can exceed."
- quote: "time-limit tests keep their wide bounds"
- quote: "with `NIO_PERF=1` set, they assert their 2-second limits as today"
- situation (logic): a review runs the full suite on a loaded machine and `NIO_PERF=1` is set in the environment. Status over 20 efforts takes 2.5 seconds, the 2-second assertion fires, and the review fails. FR-11 forbids that outcome and FR-15 allows it. The same applies to the "wide bounds" tests. A wide bound is still a wall-clock limit that enough load can exceed, so FR-11 forbids it too. AC-14 does not say that `NIO_PERF` is unset, and AC-18 does not say a review never sets it.
- situation (testability): any time limit can be exceeded under enough load, so "any wall-clock limit that load can exceed" has no pass or fail condition. AC-14 does not say how 2.5 s is produced (a sleep injected into status? a patched clock?). Nor does it say whether `NIO_PERF` is unset in that run. If `NIO_PERF=1` is inherited, the 2-second test fails by design. SC-5 ("when the machine is idle") cannot be checked either.
- situation (consistency): FR-11 says a review must never depend on a limit load can exceed, and FR-15 only moves "speed requirement" limits behind NIO_PERF. Under the Decisions bullet, a "time-limit" test with a wide bound (for example a 10-second assertion in the suite) keeps running on every review. On a loaded machine it can fail and spend a task attempt, which is the failure US-5 exists to stop. The spec never defines the split between "speed requirement" and "time-limit" tests, so a builder can't tell which side a test falls on.
- fix: reword FR-11 as "without any wall-clock assertion unless `NIO_PERF=1`". Say the review never sets `NIO_PERF`. Say what a wide-bound test is allowed to assert.
- validation: confirmed: FR-11 forbids any load-exceedable wall-clock limit, while FR-15 and the Decisions keep a 2-second limit under `NIO_PERF=1` and "wide bounds" on other time-limit tests. Nothing says a review runs with `NIO_PERF` unset, so FR-11 and FR-15 can conflict.
- disposition: spec-fix by agent: Delegated grill (human: run the whole flow on recommended): FR-11 now says the review strips NIO_PERF; FR-15 names only test_nfr3_status_speed; the 'wide bounds' decision is gone and time-limit tests are a non-goal.

### J-9 FR-15 leaves the approved 2-second status requirement unchecked by default
- quote: "US-5 changes how flow-state's NFR-3 (status in under 2 seconds, [human] in an approved spec) is checked"
- quote: "THE SYSTEM SHALL assert its time limit only when `NIO_PERF=1` is set."
- situation (logic): NFR-3 is an invariant the human approved. After this change, no default run checks it. If status takes 10 seconds, the whole suite passes unless someone sets `NIO_PERF=1`. The spec does not say who sets it or when, so NFR-3 can be broken with every test green. This is accepted in Risks but not closed by any requirement or AC.
- situation (adversary): after this change the status-speed and drift-speed limits are never asserted in the default run. No AC, FR or entry says where `NIO_PERF=1` is run (CI, a scheduled run, before release). A 10x slowdown of `nio flow status` then passes every review and gate, and the "NFR-3: status in under 2 seconds" requirement quietly loses its only check.
- fix: name where `NIO_PERF=1` runs, for example a release check or a CI job. Or add an AC that something outside the per-task review still enforces the limit.
- validation: confirmed: FR-15 and C-261105-6rme say NFR-3 "is checked on request", but no FR, AC or Decisions entry names where or when `NIO_PERF=1` runs. A 10x slowdown of status passes every default run, and the Risks bullet only asks for the change request, which is filed.
- disposition: spec-fix by agent: Delegated grill (human: run the whole flow on recommended): FR-18, AC-29: CLAUDE.md lists NIO_PERF=1 uv run python tests/test_flow.py, run after a change to nio flow status.

### J-15 FR-7 "no lens re-run" clause has no AC
- quote: "without making a lens re-run on that alone"

- situation (testability): AC-9 only checks that T-30 appears in the `nio jury changed` output. AC-10 only covers an approved gate and a status check. FR-8 covers only an add under Fixes, so it does not say whether that removal withdraws the approval.
- fix: add an AC with a fixture where the only change since the last round is a Fixes task. The Observable should be that the set of lenses due to re-run is empty (or unchanged from before).

### J-18 AC-13 judges a real model from a single run
- quote: "when the evaluator rates it on a real model"
- situation (testability): a model that is non-deterministic can pass one run and rewrite epic headings on the next. One green e2e run does not show FR-9 holds. The same run could also fail because the model rated nothing, since the AC only says changed lines must be rating lines, not that any were changed. That is a vacuous pass.

An edit tool can still change any line, such as a task's `Test:` or `Files:` line. Edits keyed on a repeated `Tier: standard` line can also land on the wrong task silently.

An empty diff, where nothing was rated, satisfies it, and it names a single real-model run (Level: e2e). Nothing else in the spec (FR-9, FR-10, SC-4) adds a non-empty requirement or a deterministic check on the diff.
- disposition: spec-fix by agent: Delegated grill (human: run the whole flow on recommended): AC-13 (one real-model run) retired; FR-9 is now a deterministic nio check tasks --rated-from <copy> (AC-26, AC-27), run by the tasks skill (FR-17, AC-28).

### J-22 A deferred TC the task partly proves drops the task's own file check
- quote: "THE SYSTEM SHALL require only the files of the TC IDs the task's `Test:` line does not say a later task proves."
- quote: "A TC a later task proves only in part counts as deferred"
- situation (consistency): take T-4 with `Test:` "TC-38 proved later by T-11", where T-4 proves half of TC-38 and T-11 proves the rest. The decision table row "deferred | - | → not required" applies, so red is accepted with no file for the part T-4 does prove, and the check in FR-12 passes because T-11 is named. A red for T-4's own half can then pass on a test that doesn't exercise it.

The decision table row "deferred | - | → not required" follows from it, and FR-12 still checks that the named later task cites the TC. The outcome the finding describes is the stated trade-off, not an unnoticed gap.

### J-23 AC-14 doesn't say whether the review runs with NIO_PERF set
- quote: "when the task's review runs the full suite, then the review passes."
- quote: "assert its time limit only when `NIO_PERF=1` is set."
- situation (consistency): the spec never says whether a task's review sets or clears NIO_PERF. If the review environment already has NIO_PERF=1 (set in a dev shell or CI), then on a slow machine the status run is 2.5 seconds, the 2-second limit applies, and AC-14 fails, which contradicts its stated pass.
- fix: state that the review runs with NIO_PERF unset, and add that case to AC-14.
- disposition: spec-fix by agent: Delegated grill (human: run the whole flow on recommended): FR-11 and AC-14: the review strips NIO_PERF, with NIO_PERF=1 in the orchestrator's environment as the case.
